Where none of those applies and the transfer rests instead on the organization’s compelling legitimate interests, the stricter conditions are checked and met - the transfer is not repetitive, concerns only a limited number of people, is necessary for interests not overridden by theirs, and all the circumstances have been assessed and suitable safeguards provided on the strength of that assessment - the supervisory authority is informed of the transfer, the people affected are told about it and about the interests pursued in addition to the ordinary information they are owed, and the assessment and the safeguards are documented in the record of processing activities rather than in a memo nobody can find.

controls.name: Binding corporate rules
controls.description: Where a group of companies moves personal data between its members across borders on the strength of binding corporate rules, those rules are a document with required content rather than a statement of intent, and the organization can show it against the list. They specify the structure and contact details of the group and of each member; the transfers or sets of transfer they cover, with the categories of personal data, the types and purposes of processing, the types of people affected and the countries involved; that they are legally binding both inside the group and externally; how the general data-protection principles are applied - purpose limitation, minimizing what is held, limited storage periods, data quality, protection by design and by default, the legal basis for processing, the handling of special category data, the measures securing the data, and what is required of any onward transfer to a body the rules do not bind; the rights of the people whose data it is and how to exercise them, including the right not to be subject to a solely automated decision, the right to complain to the competent supervisory authority and to go to court, and the route to redress and, where appropriate, compensation for a breach of the rules; the acceptance by the group member established in the region of liability for breaches by any member outside it; how the people affected are told about the rules, in addition to the ordinary information they are owed; the tasks of the data protection officer or of whoever else monitors compliance with the rules, including monitoring training and complaint handling; the complaint procedures; the mechanisms for verifying compliance, which include data protection audits and methods of ensuring corrective action, with results reported to the person who monitors the rules and to the board of the controlling undertaking and available to the supervisory authority on request; how changes to the rules are recorded, reported internally and reported to the authority; how any legal requirement in a third country that is likely to have a substantial adverse effect on the guarantees the rules provide is reported to the competent authority; and the data protection training given to personnel with permanent or regular access to personal data. The rules are submitted for approval before they are relied on, and they are maintained afterwards - reviewed as the group changes, with each change reported through the mechanism the rules themselves establish.

controls.name: Management system roles, responsibilities & authorities
controls.description: Top management assigns the responsibilities and authorities for every role the management system depends on, communicates them to the people who hold them, and satisfies itself that they are understood rather than merely issued - understanding being established by asking, not inferred from an absence of questions. The assignment is written against named roles rather than named individuals, so it survives a departure, and it carries authority alongside duty: what the role may decide alone, what it must escalate, and to whom. Five assignments are made explicitly, because they are the ones most often left in the gap between functions. Someone is responsible for the management system conforming to the standard it is built against. Someone is responsible for the processes delivering the outputs they were designed to deliver. Someone is responsible for reporting on how the system is performing, and on the opportunities to improve it, to top management itself rather than to a layer beneath it. Someone is responsible for promoting focus on the customer across the organization. And someone is responsible for the integrity of the system being maintained when changes to it are planned and implemented, so a reorganization does not quietly dismantle a control nobody was watching. The assignments are reviewed when the organization changes, and the record is kept current rather than reconstructed at audit.

controls.name: Infrastructure for operating processes
controls.description: The infrastructure the organization’s processes need in order to run, and to produce products and services that conform, is determined, provided, and then maintained rather than provided once and left to decay. What counts as infrastructure is stated rather than assumed: the buildings the work happens in and the utilities that serve them; equipment, including both the hardware and the software it runs; transportation, where moving people, materials or outputs is part of delivering the service; and the information and communication technology the processes depend on. Each is determined from what the processes actually require, so a shortfall reads as a shortfall against a named process rather than as a general complaint about the estate. Maintenance is planned rather than reactive - what is serviced, on what interval, by whom, and what evidence is kept - and provision is revisited when the volume, the mix or the location of the work changes, so infrastructure sized for what the organization used to do is not still carrying what it does now.

controls.name: Environment for the operation of processes
controls.description: The environment the organization’s processes are operated in is determined, provided and maintained as a condition of the output conforming, not as a matter of comfort. It is treated as a combination of human and physical factors, and the organization says which of them matter to which process. Social factors - whether the work is non-discriminatory, calm and non-confrontational - psychological factors - whether it is stress-reducing, protects against burnout, and is emotionally supportive - and physical factors - temperature, heat, humidity, light, airflow, hygiene, noise - are each considered, and the ones a given process is genuinely sensitive to are specified with the range or condition that has to hold. What is specified is then provided and monitored rather than aspired to, and the specification is revisited when the process, the output or the workforce changes. Which factors are relevant differs sharply with what is being delivered, so the determination is made per process rather than issued once for the whole organization.

controls.name: Monitoring & measuring resources
controls.description: Where the organization monitors or measures something in order to verify that products and services conform to requirements, the resources it uses to do so are determined and provided rather than borrowed, and they are chosen to be suitable for the specific type of monitoring or measurement being carried out - so an instrument with the wrong range, resolution or tolerance is caught at selection rather than in a dispute. Once provided, they are maintained so that they stay fit for their purpose: serviced, checked, protected from damage and from deterioration in use and in storage, and withdrawn when they are no longer fit. What the organization holds is recorded, with what each item is used for and who is responsible for it. Evidence that the resources are fit for their purpose is retained as documented information rather than asserted at audit, and it is retained for as long as the measurements they produced are relied on, not only for the current year.

controls.name: Measurement traceability & calibration
controls.description: Where measurement traceability is a requirement - because a regulation, a contract, a customer or the organization’s own judgment makes it one - measuring equipment is tied back to something outside itself. It is calibrated or verified, or both, at defined intervals and before use, against measurement standards traceable to international or national measurement standards; where no such standard exists, the basis actually used for the calibration or verification is retained as documented information, so an in-house reference is a stated basis rather than a gap. Every item carries its status, identified so that anyone picking it up can tell whether its calibration is current. It is safeguarded from adjustment, damage or deterioration that would invalidate the calibration status and the measurement results that follow from it. And when equipment is later found unfit for its purpose, the organization does not stop at fixing the equipment: it determines whether the validity of previous measurement results has been adversely affected, and takes appropriate action on the product or service those results released, up to and including recall.

controls.name: Organizational knowledge
controls.description: The knowledge the organization needs in order to operate its processes and achieve conformity of products and services is determined, held, and made available to the people who need it, instead of living in whoever happens to still work here. What is determined covers both sources. Internal knowledge: what was learned from failures and from successful projects, the undocumented expertise of experienced people, intellectual property, and the improvements captured from changes to processes, products and services. External knowledge: standards, academic and professional bodies, conferences, and what customers and external providers know. It is maintained rather than accumulated - reviewed for whether it is still correct, and held in a form the roles that need it can actually reach at the moment they need it. When needs and trends change, the organization considers its current knowledge against the change and determines how it will acquire or access whatever additional knowledge is required, including what it will do about a body of knowledge that is about to leave with a person.

controls.name: Design & development process
controls.description: Where the requirements for what the organization will provide are not already fixed by the customer or by an external specification, the organization establishes, implements and maintains a design and development process, and its extent is appropriate to what is being designed and to what would follow if the design were wrong. The process is a defined route from a stated need to a specification that can be delivered against - named stages, entry and exit conditions, and an owner - rather than an informal habit that produces a drawing. It is written down, applied to every product and service that goes through design, and maintained as the organization’s offering changes. Where the organization concludes that design and development does not apply to it, because it produces to a customer’s specification or resells what others design, that conclusion is recorded with the reason it holds, so an absent process is a stated decision instead of an unexplained gap.

controls.name: Design & development planning
controls.description: The stages of a design and the controls applied at each of them are planned before the design work starts, and the plan is proportionate to what is being designed. In deciding it, the organization considers the nature, duration and complexity of the design activity; the process stages required, including the design reviews that will be held; the verification and validation activities that will be performed and where in the sequence each of them falls; the responsibilities and authorities involved; the internal and external resources the design will need; the interfaces between the people and the functions involved, and how those interfaces will be controlled so that a handoff is not a hole; whether customers or users need to be involved and how; what will be required for the subsequent provision of the product or service, so the design is planned against how it will be made and delivered; the level of control the customer and other relevant interested parties expect over the design; and the documented information needed to confirm afterwards that the design requirements were met. The plan is documented, and it is revised when the design changes shape rather than left as the version written at kickoff.

controls.name: Design & development inputs
controls.description: What a design has to satisfy is determined and recorded before the design is worked up, and it is determined at the level of specificity the type of product or service requires rather than as a statement of intent. The inputs cover the functional and performance requirements the output must meet; information derived from previous design activity of a similar kind, so a known failure is not designed in again; the statutory and regulatory requirements that apply; standards or codes of practice the organization has committed to implement; and the potential consequences of failure given the nature of the product or service. Inputs are checked for being adequate for the purpose, complete and unambiguous, and any conflict between them is resolved before the design proceeds rather than settled implicitly by whoever builds it. The inputs are retained as documented information, so what the design was supposed to do can be established later without relying on memory.

controls.name: Design & development controls
controls.description: The design is controlled while it is being produced, so that a defect is found while it is still cheap. Four things are done and kept distinct. The results the design is to achieve are defined, so there is a stated target to judge against. Reviews are conducted at the planned points to evaluate whether the design results meet the requirements. Verification is carried out to establish that the design outputs meet the design inputs - the right answer to the question that was asked. And validation is carried out to establish that the resulting product or service meets the requirements for the specified application or intended use, where that is known - the right question. Where any of these finds a problem, action is taken on it and tracked to closure rather than noted. The reviews, the verification and the validation have distinct purposes and may be run together on a single occasion, provided the record shows which of the three each finding came from. Documented information on all of these activities, and on the actions they produced, is retained.

controls.name: Design & development outputs
controls.description: What a design produces is checked against four separate tests before it is handed on, and the check is recorded rather than assumed from the design having finished. The outputs meet the input requirements that were determined for the design, so the thing built answers the question that was asked. They are adequate for the processes that follow - purchasing, production, service delivery and the maintenance of the product after it is delivered - which means each of those functions can work from what it is given without inventing the part that is missing. They include or reference the monitoring and measuring requirements that apply, and the criteria by which an output is accepted or rejected, so acceptance is a stated threshold instead of a judgment made at the point of release. And they specify the characteristics of the product or service that are essential for its intended purpose and for its safe and proper provision, including the ones that carry a safety or regulatory consequence if they drift. Outputs are issued in a form that lets verification and validation actually be performed against them - a drawing, specification, formulation, parts list, test method, work instruction, or service definition that somebody other than the designer can test - rather than as a description that can only be judged by the person who wrote it. They are approved by a role entitled to approve them before they are released to the next stage, and documented information on the outputs is retained, so what the design actually specified can be established later against what was made.

controls.name: Design & development changes
controls.description: A change made to a design - during the design work, or afterwards once the product or service is already being provided - is identified as a change, reviewed, and controlled to the extent necessary to ensure it does not adversely affect conformity to requirements. The review asks what else the change touches: the inputs it invalidates, the verification and validation that has to be repeated, the documentation and the downstream processes that have to move with it. The change is authorized by a role entitled to authorize it before it takes effect. Documented information is retained on the changes themselves, on the results of the review, on the authorization of the change, and on the actions taken to prevent an adverse effect - so a change is answerable afterwards rather than visible only as a difference between two versions.

controls.name: Control of production & service provision
controls.description: Production and the provision of services are carried out under conditions the organization has defined in advance and can show were in place, rather than under whatever conditions the day produced. Those conditions are stated: documented information defining the characteristics of what is to be produced, the service to be provided or the activity to be performed, and the results to be achieved; suitable monitoring and measuring resources available and actually used; monitoring and measurement carried out at the appropriate stages to verify that the criteria for control of processes and the criteria for acceptance of outputs have been met; suitable infrastructure and a suitable environment for the operation of the processes; competent people, including any qualification the work requires; validation, and periodic revalidation, of any process whose resulting output cannot be verified by later monitoring or measurement, because the only alternative is discovering the failure in use; and actions designed to prevent human error - a check, a forcing function, a second pair of eyes - rather than an instruction to be careful. Release, delivery and post-delivery activities are carried out under the same defined conditions.

controls.name: Identification & traceability of outputs
controls.description: Outputs are identified by suitable means wherever identification is necessary to ensure the conformity of products and services, so that what something is - and which batch, order or version it belongs to - can be established without inference. The status of an output with respect to monitoring and measurement requirements is identified throughout production and service provision, so a unit that has not yet passed a check cannot be mistaken for one that has, at any point in the flow. And where traceability is a requirement, whether imposed by a regulator, a customer, a contract or the organization’s own risk judgment, the unique identification of the outputs is controlled and the documented information necessary to enable traceability is retained - so that from a delivered item the organization can work back to what went into it, and forward from a defect to everything else affected by it.

controls.name: Care of customer & external provider property
controls.description: Property belonging to a customer or to an external provider is treated with care for the whole time it is under the organization’s control or in use by it, and the organization knows what it holds. Property here is not only physical: it includes materials, components, tools and equipment, premises made available for the work, intellectual property, and personal data. Each item is identified, verified on receipt against what was expected, and then protected and safeguarded against loss, against damage, and against use for anything other than what it was provided for. When any of it is lost, damaged, or otherwise found to be unsuitable for use, the organization reports that to its owner rather than absorbing it quietly, and retains documented information on what happened and on what was reported. Where the property is personal data, the handling obligations the organization is already under apply to it in addition to this duty rather than instead of it.

controls.name: Preservation of outputs
controls.description: Outputs are preserved during production and service provision to the extent necessary for them still to conform to requirements when they reach the customer, so that something made correctly is not delivered spoiled. Preservation is treated as covering the whole handling chain rather than storage alone: identification, handling, contamination control, packaging, storage, transmission or transportation, and protection. What each output actually needs is determined from what would degrade it - time, temperature, humidity, light, static, vibration or contamination, and in the case of information, corruption and unauthorized alteration - and the conditions are then specified, provided and checked rather than assumed from the warehouse being indoors. Preservation applies to the constituent parts of a product as well as to the finished output, so a component held badly is caught before it is built in.

controls.name: Control of changes to production & service provision
controls.description: A change to how something is produced, or to how a service is provided, is reviewed and controlled to the extent necessary to keep what is delivered conforming to its requirements - a new machine, a new material, a new supplier of a component, a new step, a new location, a new shift pattern, or a change to the people who do the work. The review establishes what the change would do to the output and to the process controls that protect it, and whether any verification or validation has to be repeated before the change takes effect. Documented information is retained describing the results of the review, the person or persons who authorized the change, and any necessary actions arising from the review - so the change has an owner and a rationale on the record rather than an effective date alone.

controls.name: Release of products & services
controls.description: Nothing is released to the customer until the organization has verified that the requirements for the product or service have been met. Release is a decision taken against planned arrangements, at the stages those arrangements set, and it does not proceed until those arrangements have been satisfactorily completed - unless it is otherwise approved by a relevant authority and, where applicable, by the customer, which is a documented exception rather than a routine. The organization retains documented information on the release: evidence of conformity with the acceptance criteria the output was judged against, and traceability to the person or persons who authorized the release, so a released item can be tied back to the individual who signed for it.

controls.name: Monitoring & measurement of quality performance
controls.description: What the organization needs to monitor and measure in order to know whether it is performing and whether its quality management system is effective is decided in advance and written down, together with three further decisions that are usually left implicit: the methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation that will be used, chosen so that they produce valid results rather than convenient ones; when the monitoring and measuring is to be performed; and when the results are to be analyzed and evaluated, which is a separate date from when they are collected. What is chosen reaches the conformity of products and services and the effectiveness of the system, not activity counts that are easy to produce. Documented information is retained as evidence of the results, so a measurement can be re-examined rather than only reported, and the set of things being measured is revisited when what the organization does, or what it is judged on, changes.

controls.name: Analysis & evaluation of quality data
controls.description: The data and information that monitoring and measurement produce are analyzed and evaluated rather than filed, and the results are used to answer a fixed set of questions: whether products and services conform to requirements; the degree of customer satisfaction; how the quality management system is performing and whether it is effective; whether what was planned has been implemented effectively; whether the actions taken to address risks and opportunities were effective; how external providers are performing; and whether the system itself needs to be improved. The analysis distinguishes a trend from a single reading and states the basis on which it does so, and the evaluation is written as a conclusion with a consequence - what this means, and what should follow - rather than as a chart with no reader. The results are carried into management review and into the improvement process as inputs of record, rather than as slides prepared for a meeting.

controls.name: Sensitive authentication data not retained
controls.description: The data a card presents in order to prove the card itself is genuine - the full contents of the magnetic stripe or its equivalent held on the chip, the verification code printed on or encoded into the card, and the PIN or the encrypted PIN block - is not kept once the transaction has been authorized. That holds everywhere it could come to rest and not only in the payment database: application and debug logs, request and response traces, message queues, error dumps and crash reports, support tickets and attachments, screenshots, analytics events, backups, and the file a developer copied in order to reproduce a problem. Where any of it genuinely has to be held before authorization, it is held only for as long as authorization takes, is protected with strong cryptography while it is there, is readable by the smallest set of people and services that can complete the work, and is removed by the process itself rather than by somebody remembering. The verification code is not kept after authorization in any form, encrypted included, because encryption changes who can read a value and not whether the organization is still holding it. Copies are searched for rather than assumed absent: the systems and stores in scope are examined on a defined cadence and after any change to the payment flow, what is found is securely destroyed and the destruction recorded, and the route that produced it - a verbose log level, a captured request, a helpful export - is closed so the same copy does not reappear next month.

controls.name: Card number display masking
controls.description: The full card number is not the default thing a screen shows. Displays are masked so that what appears is the smallest fragment that lets somebody do the job in front of them, and seeing more than that is a separately authorized act: the roles with a documented business need for the whole number are listed, each holder is approved individually, and the need is reviewed rather than inherited. Everybody else sees the masked form, and sees it whether or not their access would technically let them read the underlying record, because the masking is applied by the system rather than left to the discretion of whoever built the screen. It applies everywhere the number can be read and not only in the main application: administrative and support tooling, reports and dashboards, exports and extracts, printed and emailed documents, receipts, and anything shown to a third party. Where the number is reached through a remote-access technology - a published desktop or application, a support session, a screen-sharing tool, a virtual workspace - technical controls prevent it from being copied, downloaded or relocated onto the local machine unless the person is explicitly authorized and a documented business need says why, so a session that legitimately displays the data does not quietly become a route to a copy of it. Where a masking rule is relaxed for a person, a role or a screen, the relaxation is recorded with the need behind it, an owner and an expiry, and is reviewed on a cadence rather than left standing.

controls.name: Public-facing web application protection
controls.description: An application the organization publishes to the internet carries a protection that runs continuously in front of it rather than a check that happened once. An automated technical solution sits ahead of each public-facing web application, inspecting the traffic that reaches it and detecting and preventing the web-based attacks the organization has decided it must withstand - injection, tampering with parameters and sessions, abuse of an authenticated function, and whatever classes its own findings and the wider threat picture put in front of it. It is actively running rather than installed, is kept current as new attack patterns are published, produces audit records that are retained and read, and is configured either to block what it detects or to raise an alert a named role acts on immediately - a decision taken deliberately for each application rather than left wherever the product shipped it. Coverage is answerable from the estate rather than from memory: the internet-facing applications are inventoried, each is matched to the protection standing in front of it, and one with no protection is a finding with an owner and a date rather than an omission nobody owns. New threats and vulnerabilities affecting these applications are tracked as they emerge and the application and its protection are updated for them. Where the organization runs assessment alongside that mechanism, that assessment runs on a stated cadence and again after every significant change, is performed by people or tools competent to do it, and its findings are remediated and retested rather than reported.

controls.name: Payment terminal protection
controls.description: The devices a customer physically presents a card to are protected against being tampered with or swapped, because a terminal is the part of the payment path an attacker can reach with their hands. The organization keeps a current list of every such device in its care - make and model, location, serial or other unique identifier, and the person answerable for it - and updates the list when a device is added, moved, returned or retired. Devices are inspected against that list on a stated recurring cadence, and the inspection looks for what actually happens: a serial number that no longer matches, a housing or seal that has been opened, a cable, overlay, reader or attachment that was not there before, a device substituted while nobody was watching, and changes to the surroundings that would let somebody observe a PIN being entered. What each inspection found, when, and who performed it is recorded rather than confirmed verbally. The staff who work with the devices are trained for the part only they can do: to verify the identity and the authorization of anybody claiming to install, service, replace or inspect a device before letting them near one, to refuse an unexpected visit and check it against a known contact, to recognize behavior around a terminal that does not belong, and to know exactly who to tell and how quickly. Devices held in stock, in transit or awaiting repair are controlled on the same terms as devices in use, and a device suspected of tampering is taken out of service under a documented route rather than left running while somebody decides.

controls.name: Payment page script integrity
controls.description: Every script that a customer’s browser loads and runs on a page where payment details are entered is known, justified and watched, because that page executes in an environment the organization does not control. Each script is inventoried with what it does, why it is needed and who authorized it, and one nobody can justify is removed rather than left because it has always been there - including the scripts that arrive indirectly, through a tag manager, an analytics package, a chat or support widget, or as a dependency of another script. The integrity of each is assured by a mechanism the organization can evidence, such as pinning it to a known hash, constraining what the page is permitted to load, serving it from somewhere the organization controls, or an equivalent chosen deliberately and written down. What the browser actually receives is then checked on a defined cadence - weekly, unless a documented targeted risk analysis supports a different one - covering both the scripts the page loads and the HTTP headers it returns, and compared against what was authorized. A change nobody approved raises an alert to a named role who investigates it as a possible compromise rather than as a release note, and the check itself is monitored, so a check that has silently stopped running is noticed rather than trusted.

controls.name: Service provider responsibility acknowledgement
controls.description: Where the organization holds, processes or transmits payment or account data on behalf of its customers, it says so to them in writing rather than leaving the division of duty to be inferred from a contract about something else. The acknowledgement states that the organization is responsible for the security of the data it holds on the customer’s behalf, and for anything within its service that could affect the security of the customer’s own environment; it is given before the service starts and given again when the service changes materially. Alongside it the organization maintains a written division of responsibility - which requirements it meets on the customer’s behalf, which remain the customer’s, and which are shared and in what proportion - specific enough that a customer can see what it still has to do rather than being told the service is compliant and left to guess. Evidence of the organization’s own standing is kept current and provided on request: the assessment or attestation it holds, its date, what it covers and what falls outside it. Requests from customers for any of this go to a named owner and are answered within a stated time, and the organization tells affected customers when its own standing changes rather than waiting to be asked at renewal.

controls.name: Age restriction on creator content above the app’s rating
controls.description: Where an app presents material authored by a community of non-developer creators rather than by the developer itself, two things are built rather than assumed. First, a user can tell which of that content exceeds the app’s own age rating: the rating of each item is carried through to the place where a user chooses it - the feed, the browse or search result, the channel or profile page, the thumbnail - so a parent or an older user sees the difference before opening it rather than afterwards. Second, an age restriction mechanism acts on an age signal, verified or declared, to keep underage users out of the creator content that exceeds the rating, so the labeling is enforced rather than merely displayed. The mechanism covers every route into that content, including a direct link, a share, an embed and a recommendation, because a gate on the browse surface alone is not a restriction. What the mechanism does when there is no age signal at all is decided in advance and written down rather than defaulting to access, and a creator item whose rating has never been established is treated under that same written rule rather than as unrated-therefore-open.

controls.name: Age restriction on non-embedded software above the app’s rating
controls.description: Where an app offers software that is not embedded in its own binary - HTML5 and JavaScript mini apps and mini games, streaming games, chatbots, plug-ins, and retro console or PC emulators offering downloadable titles - two things are built rather than assumed. First, a user can tell which of that software exceeds the app’s own age rating: each title carries its rating through to the place where a user launches or installs it, including the in-app store or catalog, the search result and the recommendation, so the difference is visible before the software runs rather than after. Second, an age restriction mechanism acts on an age signal, verified or declared, to keep underage users out of the software that exceeds the rating, and it acts at launch rather than only at listing, so a deep link, a shared invite or a resumed session does not bypass it. The rating relied on for each title is recorded with where it came from - the developer’s own classification, the third-party publisher’s, or a rating body’s - so a title running without an established rating is a finding with an owner rather than an omission, and it is handled under the written rule for what the mechanism does when a rating or an age signal is absent instead of defaulting to access.

controls.name: Human review of ad creative for age appropriateness
controls.description: Every advertisement that can be displayed to a child is reviewed by a person for whether it suits that audience before it is allowed to run, and the review is recorded against the creative it approved. This is a duty on the developer rather than a question about the ad vendor, and it reaches creative no third-party network ever touched: the app’s own house ads, cross-promotions for the developer’s other titles, sponsor placements sold directly, and anything served through a partner or a mediation layer. Where creative does arrive from an ad service, the service’s own human review is evidenced from its published practices rather than assumed from its reputation, and the developer still keeps its own record of what it accepted. Approval is per creative rather than per campaign, an approved creative is reviewed again when it changes, and there is a stated route to pull one that is already running.

controls.name: Alternative sign-in for users under 13
controls.description: Where an app authenticates an account using facial recognition, a user under 13 can sign in another way. Two things follow and both are built: the app holds an age signal at account level, so it knows which accounts the alternative is owed to, and a working fallback credential exists and is tested rather than assumed - an account that can only be opened by a face is unusable by exactly the users this exists for. The alternative is offered rather than hidden behind a support request: it appears on the sign-in path itself, and choosing it does not cost the user functionality the face route would have given them. Where the app cannot establish an age, it treats the account as one that needs the alternative rather than one that does not. This is a control over the route into an account, and it is separate from any consent or data-handling duty the biometric feature itself attracts.

controls.name: Consent from human subject research participants
controls.description: An app that conducts health-related human subject research obtains consent from each participant before enrolling them, and where the participant is a minor that consent comes from a parent or guardian rather than from the minor. The consent covers a fixed set of things and is evidenced as having covered them: the nature, purpose and duration of the research; the procedures involved and the risks and benefits to the participant; how confidentiality and the data will be handled, including any sharing with third parties; a point of contact for the participant’s questions; and how a participant withdraws. Each is recorded as it was actually presented rather than as it was intended, so a change to the protocol, or to who receives the data, is a change to what was consented to and triggers consent again. The withdrawal route is operable rather than described: a request reaches a named owner, further collection stops, and what happens to data already collected is stated to the participant in advance instead of decided afterwards. This is consent to take part in research, and it is not the same act as verifiable parental consent to collect a child’s personal information - an app doing both performs both.

controls.name: Restricted platform permissions in children’s apps
controls.description: Where a store requires a device capability to be requested through a specific, narrower platform API rather than through the broad permission, the app calls that API. Google Play requires an app in its Families program to request Bluetooth through the Companion Device Manager, which binds the grant to one device the user chooses instead of giving the app open scanning access to everything nearby; the app is built that way rather than granted the broad permission and trusted to behave. The one stated way out is an app targeting only operating-system versions that cannot support the narrower API, and that is a claim the build has to bear out: the declared minimum supported version is recorded beside the exemption and re-checked whenever it is raised, because raising it takes the exemption away. Evidence is read off the app rather than off the policy - the permissions the manifest declares, the pairing flow a user actually meets, and a review of both at each release, so a permission introduced by a dependency is caught before it ships.

controls.name: Scope of the financial reporting assessment
controls.description: Before anything is tested, the organization states what the financial statements have to achieve and which parts of them the assessment covers, because a control program with no stated objective tests whatever is convenient to test. Materiality is set and the basis it was derived from is written down rather than carried over from last year. The accounts and disclosures that matter are identified, each with the reason it qualified - its size and composition, how susceptible it is to error or fraud, the volume and complexity of what flows through it, the accounting and reporting judgments it involves, its exposure to loss or to a contingent liability, whether related parties transact in it, and what has changed about it since the prior period. For each of those, the assertions genuinely at risk are named - that the balance exists and the transactions occurred, that nothing is missing, that amounts are valued or allocated correctly, that the rights and obligations are the organization’s own, and that it is presented and disclosed properly - rather than testing every assertion of every account at the same depth. The likely ways each could be misstated are recorded alongside them, which is what makes the risk work that follows specific rather than generic. The scope is revisited when the business, the accounting standards or the systems change, and what came into and out of scope is recorded with the reason, so the boundary is answerable rather than inherited.

controls.name: Financial reporting risk assessment
controls.description: Against the objective and scope already stated, the organization identifies what could cause the financial statements to be materially misstated, and does so across the whole reporting entity - the parent, its subsidiaries and divisions, the locations that roll up into the consolidation, and the third parties whose work ends up in the numbers, including outsourced processing and service providers. The sources are worked through rather than brainstormed: how the applicable accounting framework applies to the transactions this business actually enters into; how each of those is initiated, authorized, processed and recorded; the estimates and judgments management makes; and the internal and external changes that alter any of them. Each identified risk is analyzed for how likely it is and for what it would do if it happened, and every one leaves the assessment with an explicit decision on how it is being managed - a register with no response column records worry rather than management. The assessment is refreshed on a defined cadence and, separately, whenever something happens that changes it, so it is not a document produced once a year and filed. What was considered and set aside is recorded as well as what was accepted, so a later reviewer can see the boundary of the exercise instead of inferring it.

controls.name: ESG risk identification & treatment
controls.description: Environmental, social and governance risks are identified, rated and treated through the organization’s risk process rather than tracked in a separate document nobody acts on. What is looked for is stated so the exercise is repeatable: the environmental risks the operation and its supply chain create and are exposed to; the risks to and from the people the organization employs, sells to and operates among; and the governance risks that come from how it is directed, incentivized and held to account. Each risk gets a named owner, an assessment of how likely it is and what it would cost - in money, in harm to people, and in the organization’s standing - and a decided treatment with a date, and the treatments are followed up rather than merely recorded. The same criteria and the same register the organization uses for its other risks apply here, so an ESG risk is weighed against everything else competing for attention instead of considered beside it. The set is reviewed on a defined cadence and again when the operation, the supply chain, the regulatory position or the stakeholder picture changes, and what the review changed is recorded.

controls.name: Employment eligibility verification
controls.description: Every new hire’s identity and authorization to work is verified on the required form, inside the statutory window, and in a way that does not discriminate. The employee completes their own section at the time of hire; the employer examines the documentation the employee presents and completes the employer section within three business days of the hire, and where the engagement will last less than three business days, at the time of hire. Which acceptable documents to present is the employee’s choice: the employer does not specify which ones it wants, does not ask for more or different documents than the form requires, and does not refuse documents that on their face reasonably appear to be genuine and to relate to the person - demanding extra papers is itself the unlawful act rather than an inconvenience. Citizenship status and national origin play no part in whether, when or how the check is run, so the same process is applied to everyone hired. Completed forms are held so they can be produced on request within the notice an inspection carries, and kept apart from the general personnel file where that is practical. Where an authorization expires and re-verification is required, it is diarized against the date rather than noticed once it has passed, and the people who run onboarding are trained on all of this, because the discriminatory version of this control is usually performed by somebody being helpful.

controls.name: Time and pay records
controls.description: The organization creates and keeps an accurate record of the hours each non-exempt worker actually worked and the wages actually paid, because this is a duty to PRODUCE a record and not only to keep one - a period nobody wrote down cannot be reconstructed later. For each such worker the record carries who they are and the identifying details the regulations call for, the time and day of the week the workweek begins, hours worked each day and the total for each workweek, the basis on which the wages are paid, the regular hourly rate, straight-time and overtime earnings for the workweek, every addition to and deduction from wages, total wages for the pay period, and the date of payment with the period it covers. No particular form or timekeeping method is required - a clock, a timekeeper, or workers writing their own times all qualify - provided what results is complete and accurate, so the method is chosen deliberately, written down and checked rather than trusted. Payroll records are preserved for at least three years, and the records the wage computations were built from - time cards, work and time schedules, wage-rate tables, and records of additions to and deductions from wages - for at least two, held where they can be produced for inspection. A correction is made as a correction, with what changed, when and why still visible, rather than by overwriting the original.

controls.name: Break time and space for nursing employees
controls.description: A nursing employee can take the break time they need to express breast milk, as often as they need it, for one year after the child’s birth, and has somewhere to do it. The space is not a bathroom - a private one does not qualify - and it is shielded from view and free from intrusion by coworkers and the public. It has to be functional for the purpose rather than merely nominated: somewhere to sit, a surface, and availability when the employee needs it. A space that is not dedicated to this use is acceptable only where it is genuinely free at the moment it is needed, so a room that is usually occupied, or that has to be negotiated for each time, is not the space this requires. Break time is unpaid only where the employee is completely relieved of duty for it: time spent pumping while doing any work is worked time, and where the employer already provides paid breaks, an employee who uses one for this is paid for it the same way as anyone else. The arrangement is communicated to the employee and to the managers who schedule them, and requests go to a named owner, so access does not depend on an individual negotiating for it. Where an employer with fewer than 50 employees relies on the undue-hardship relief the statute allows, the hardship is assessed and recorded against the difficulty and expense in the circumstances of that business rather than asserted.

controls.name: Lie-detector testing limits
controls.description: The organization does not require, request, suggest or cause an employee or a job applicant to take a lie detector test, and does not use, accept, refer to or ask about the results of one. Nobody is discharged, disciplined, denied employment or otherwise discriminated against for refusing a test, for filing a complaint, or for taking part in a proceeding about one. The prohibition lives in hiring practice as much as in investigations, so recruiters, hiring managers and anyone who runs an internal investigation are told it exists - the request is most often made informally, by somebody who did not know they could not make it. Where the organization believes one of the narrow statutory exemptions applies - certain applicants at armored car, alarm and guard firms, certain applicants at manufacturers, distributors and dispensers of controlled substances, or an employee reasonably suspected of involvement in a workplace incident that caused a specific economic loss or injury - the decision is taken in advance by a named owner, the basis for it is written down, and the conditions attached to the exemption are met rather than assumed: an examiner who is licensed and bonded or carries professional liability coverage, the pre-test, test and post-test conduct the rules require, and the strict limits on who may be told the result. The records the statute requires are kept, and the notice it requires is posted where employees will see it.

controls.name: Lawful basis for monitoring employee communications
controls.description: Before any monitoring that could intercept an employee’s communications is switched on, the organization decides and records what makes it lawful, because federal law prohibits intercepting a wire, oral or electronic communication unless an exception applies, and a policy that merely announces monitoring is not one of them. Each monitoring practice is written down on its own - what is captured, from which systems and endpoints, whether content or only metadata, who can see it, how long it is held and what it may be used for - and each carries the basis it relies on, most commonly the prior consent of a party to the communication, or the route that turns on equipment furnished by the service provider and used in the ordinary course of business. Consent, where it is relied on, is obtained and evidenced rather than inferred from a handbook nobody signed, and it is obtained before the monitoring starts. The monitoring then stops where its basis stops: it continues only so far as the exception reaches, communications that fall outside it are not swept in by default, and a practice that has outgrown its basis is re-decided rather than quietly extended. Where employees are told how they are monitored, that notice matches what is actually done. State and local law can be stricter than the federal floor, so the basis is checked against the jurisdictions the workforce actually sits in, and a monitoring practice with no recorded basis is switched off until it has one.
